summary:
ORBIS Health is a web tool for health monitoring on long-duration space missions, organized around the five hazards of NASA's Human Research Program: space radiation, isolation and confinement, distance from Earth, gravity fields and hostile/closed environments. It lets crew members keep track of their physical and mental health onboard, and it gives the medical team on Earth the summaries and alerts they need to act.
Because communication with Earth is delayed, alerts and emergency protocols fire instantly onboard, and the app keeps working offline as an installable PWA. This matters because on missions to the Moon and Mars the crew cannot wait for real-time medical support: ORBIS Health provides that autonomy while keeping the crew's private information private.
details:
Challenge: Create Health Monitoring Software for Astronauts on Space Missions.

ORBIS Health is a web tool that helps members of a space mission keep track of their health parameters so they can be reviewed and evaluated by medical staff, either on Earth or onboard with them. An alert system raises notifications when a parameter is outside its regular range: the crew member immediately receives the matching step-by-step protocol, and the medical team is informed so they can help find a solution and bring the parameter back to normal.

Crew members see their current state in numbers and can register parameters such as vitals, radiation, sleep, exercise, nutrition and a daily wellbeing survey, so the medical staff can take the best course of action to maintain the health of everyone onboard. Medical staff see tables with a summary of each crew member and can assign them routines, exercises and medications. The app has four roles: crew member, medical officer, ground specialist (such as the psychologist) and commander.

The two sides are connected through a simulated communication delay with Earth (18 seconds in the demo, standing for 18 minutes one way). Alerts fire onboard instantly, while the ground team receives them after the delay. The app is installable as a PWA and keeps the emergency protocols available offline.

ORBIS Health also includes two modules that bridge physical and mental health in the same tool: MoveNet and ORBIS Mind.

MoveNet: on the medical console, MoveNet (TensorFlow.js) analyzes a video example of an exercise or stretch and maps the joint angles at rest and at contraction. The medical staff can assign that exercise to a crew member. The crew member then follows it with their camera, and the app (using MediaPipe Pose, running locally in the browser) checks that the exercise is being executed correctly.

ORBIS Mind: a chatbot that talks with the crew member about their emotional state, provides company and gives feedback as the conversation goes on. The topics of the conversation are used to generate a general emotional-state summary that is shown to both the crew member and the medical staff. The chat messages are stored in a private table protected by Row Level Security, so only the crew member can read them: the medical staff never see the conversation, only the derived summary, which can inform them about the state of any given crew member. Crew members can also request a private video call with the psychologist on Earth.

Space weather: using NASA's DONKI data, the app shows real space weather, calculates a radiation risk level and raises alerts that point to the shelter protocol. It can also replay a real solar energetic particle event as a drill, so the crew can practice the shelter procedure.

ORBIS Health aims to ease the communication between crew and medical staff and to help both sides keep watch on the wellbeing of everyone on the mission, giving the crew the autonomy they need when Earth is too far away to answer in time. The same clinical core could also support remote rehabilitation and monitoring of patients on Earth.

Tools: JavaScript, HTML and CSS on the frontend; Node.js with Express and Socket.io on the backend; PostgreSQL on Supabase with Row Level Security; WebRTC for video calls; Chart.js for charts; MediaPipe Pose and TensorFlow.js (MoveNet) for pose analysis; Progressive Web App (service worker) for offline use. The sensor values shown in the demo are simulated.
